To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women with abnormal cervical smears prefer treatment of high grade CIN with imiqumod to LLETZ, but only when the risk of subinfertility and premature birth in future pregnancies is low.
women with high-grade CIN prefer LLETZ over imiquimod when the risk of sub-fertility is high and imiquimod over LLETZ when the risk of premature birth is high.
women prefer a treatment of high-grade cervical intra epithelial neoplasias with LLETZ over imiquimod when the risk of sub fertility and premature birth are high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preferences of women who desire a future pregnancy and are confronted with a high-grade CIN, for a non-surgical treatment option.
the development and application of discrete choice experiment (DCE) methods to assess patient preferences for treatment options.
the preferences of women who have to choose between surgical or pharmacological treatment for CIN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice between LLETZ and imiquimod is not straightforward and depends on a number of treatment characteristics, as well as on individual preferences.
treatment of high-grade cervical dysplasia with imiquimods may be preferred over LLETZ by women with a future pregnancy desire, but only if the risk of premature birth and subfertility is low.
the choice for imiqumod treatment is influenced by the intention to have a future pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the women in our study preferred a treatment for high-grade CIN that had a high treatment success rate, low side effect rate, and a low risk of subfertitlity and premature birth in future pregnancies.

we have developed a discrete choice experiment to investigate women’s preferences regarding treatment for high-grade cervical lesions, and we have shown that women with a future pregnancy desire prefer treatment with imiquimods.
women who want a future pregnancy prefer treatment with imiquimods to LLETZ.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice for imiqumod or LLETZ treatment of high-grade cervical intra epithelial neoplasias is not straightforward and depends on the characteristics of the treatment and on the patients’ preferences.
women with abnormal cervical screening results may have preferences for treatment of their disease, which should be considered when offering treatment options.
